summary_html: Child safely **reunified with parent or guardian**, case closed. Federal policy treats reunification as the preferred outcome once risk factors are mitigated.
authority_html:
- **Adoption and Safe Families Act (ASFA)** — establishes reunification timelines and permanency goals  
- **SSA Title IV-E (42 U.S.C. §§ 670–679c)** — funds reunification services and tracks permanency outcomes

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.holding: The court held that when parental rights are terminated for palpable unfitness the district court must still determine whether reasonable efforts to rehabilitate and reunify were made, even if the determination is that services would be unrealistic.
key_cases.relevance: It anchors the reunification obligation: no termination without a judicial evaluation of the agency's rehabilitative efforts.
key_cases.quote: provision of reasonable efforts must be evaluated by the court in every case

key_cases.holding: The court reversed the court of appeals and held that the county's reasonable efforts to reunite were supported by clear and convincing evidence, explaining that reasonable efforts are assessed after statutory grounds and best interests are established.
key_cases.relevance: It defines what the county must show about its reunification efforts before permanency can be changed away from reunification.
key_cases.quote: the appellate court then determines whether there is clear and convincing evidence that the county made reasonable efforts to reunite the family

key_cases.case_name: In re Welfare of the Children of T.R.
key_cases.holding: The court held that substance or alcohol use alone does not render a parent palpably unfit and that the county's testing-only response did not amount to reasonable efforts, reversing the termination.
key_cases.relevance: Reasonable efforts toward reunification are always required until the court finds on a prima facie showing that they may cease.
key_cases.quote: substance or alcohol use alone does not render a parent palpably unfit

key_cases.case_name: In re Welfare of the Child of E.A.C.
key_cases.holding: The court held that on a challenge to an ICWA petition for return of custody the agency bears the burden of proving active efforts and the serious-damage finding beyond a reasonable doubt, and remanded for application of that standard.
key_cases.relevance: It places the burden on the county to prove beyond a reasonable doubt that active efforts were made before a parent's request to have an Indian child returned may be denied.
key_cases.quote: the burden of proof to determine whether active efforts have been made is beyond a reasonable doubt and rests with the agency responsible for providing the remedial services

key_cases.holding: Reversing the court of appeals and leaving the trial court's dismissal of the petition in place, the court held the county had not proved palpable unfitness or refusal to comply with parental duties, where it made an admission of culpability the gateway goal of its case plan while itself failing to provide the services and counseling that would have made rehabilitation possible.
key_cases.relevance: A county that has not delivered the services its own plan demands has not done what Minnesota requires before the goal of reunification may be abandoned.
key_cases.quote: The county's expectations seem especially daunting considering the county's admitted failure to provide services, counseling or assistance to aid Ostlund in coming to grips with her conduct.

key_cases.case_name: In re Welfare of the Child of W.L.P.
key_cases.holding: Affirming both terminations, the court held that a parent's admission to the allegations of an involuntary termination petition does not convert it into a voluntary termination, that a prior involuntary termination therefore triggers the presumption of palpable unfitness, and that in such cases the county is relieved of the obligation to make reasonable efforts to rehabilitate and reunify.
key_cases.relevance: It is the express carve-out from Minnesota's otherwise mandatory reunification-efforts requirement and must be read alongside S.Z. and T.R., which state the general rule.
key_cases.quote: But in cases where the court has previously terminated an individual's parental rights, reasonable efforts for rehabilitation and reunification are not required.

state_agency.name: Minnesota Department of Children, Youth, and Families
state_agency.hotline: No statewide hotline. Call the county or Tribal child protection agency where the child lives — the directory link is on dcyf.mn.gov/individuals-and-families/report-abuse

extended_foster_care_age: To age 21 (voluntary; youth must meet one of five eligibility conditions; re-entry to 21 allowed; Minn. Stat. § 260C.451)

common_failures: Failure to prove unfitness by clear and convincing evidence
Santosky v. Kramer standard not met

timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: Must file TPR or document compelling reason

timeline_requirements.starts_from: The child's placement out of the home of the parent or guardian from whom the child was removed
timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: Not specified in Minn. Stat. § 260C.204; subd. 1 requires the court to hold the permanency progress hearing no later than six months after the child's placement, and subd. 4(a)(2) lets the court continue the matter no more than six additional months before a hearing under §§ 260C.503 to 260C.521.
